subject: Mathematics
title: Trigonometric Functions
learningOutcomes: Find the domain and range of the six trigonometric functions and of simple expressions built from them
Recognise a periodic function and find the period of \(a\sin(bx+c)\), \(a\tan(bx+c)\), their reciprocals, powers and sums
Find the maximum and minimum values of \(a+b\sin\theta\), \(a+b\cos\theta\), \(a+b\sin(c\theta+d)\) and \(a+b\cos(c\theta+d)\)
Find the maximum and minimum values (or the range) of the reciprocals of these functions
Graph \(y=a\sin bx\), \(y=a\cos bx\) and the six basic functions, and state the properties of each graph
Decide whether a trigonometric function is even, odd or neither
Write a sinusoidal model \(y=a\cos(bt)+d\) or \(a\sin(bt)+d\) from a description (maximum, minimum, period, starting point)
Use a sinusoidal model to answer questions about heights, times and voltages (Ferris wheel, AC supply)
Find the greatest and least value of \(a\cos x+b\sin x\) using \(R=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) (W.H. addition)

sections.heading: Reading the Unit 9 Picture
sections.body: Every trigonometric function is a wave read off the unit circle. For \(y=a\,f[b(x-c)]+d\), four numbers control everything: \(a\) stretches the wave up and down (amplitude \(|a|\)), \(b\) squeezes it sideways (period \(2\pi/b\) for sin and cos), \(c\) slides it left or right, and \(d\) lifts it up or down (the midline).

sections.heading: Domain and Range (9.1)
sections.body: Sine and cosine are defined for all real \(x\) with range \([-1,1]\). Tangent has domain \(x\ne(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) and range \(\mathbb R\); cotangent has domain \(x\ne n\pi\) and range \(\mathbb R\). Secant (zeros of cos excluded) and cosecant (zeros of sin excluded) have range \(|y|\ge1\), that is \((-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\).

sections.heading: Periodic Functions (9.2)
sections.body: A function is periodic if \(f(x+p)=f(x)\) for all \(x\); the period is the smallest positive \(p\). \(\sin\), \(\cos\), \(\sec\), \(\csc\) have period \(2\pi\); \(\tan\) and \(\cot\) have period \(\pi\). If \(f\) has period \(p\) then \(f(ax+b)\) has period \(p/|a|\); the coefficient and the shift outside do not matter.

sections.heading: Period of a Sum, Powers (9.2)
sections.body: For \(f+g\) write both periods as fractions: the period of the sum is the LCM of the numerators over the HCF of the denominators. Even powers and absolute values of sin and cos (\(\sin^2x\), \(|\cos x|\)) have period \(\pi\); odd powers keep \(2\pi\); every power of tan has period \(\pi\).

sections.heading: Maximum and Minimum (9.3)
sections.body: For \(y=a+b\sin(c\theta+d)\) or \(a+b\cos(c\theta+d)\) the maximum is \(a+|b|\) and the minimum is \(a-|b|\); \(c\) and \(d\) do not change them. Equivalently, midline \(=\frac{M+m}{2}\) and amplitude \(=\frac{M-m}{2}\).

sections.heading: Reciprocal Functions (9.3)
sections.body: To find the extreme values of \(1/g(\theta)\), first find the maximum \(M\) and minimum \(m\) of \(g\). If \(M\) and \(m\) have the same sign, the new maximum is \(1/m\) and the new minimum is \(1/M\). If they have opposite signs, \(g\) passes through zero and there is no maximum or minimum.

sections.heading: Graphs (9.4)
sections.body: Draw one period and repeat it. For \(y=a\sin bx\) the five key points on one period \(T=2\pi/b\) are at \(0,\ T/4,\ T/2,\ 3T/4,\ T\), with heights \(0,\ a,\ 0,\ -a,\ 0\); for cosine they are \(a,\ 0,\ -a,\ 0,\ a\). Tangent and cotangent have vertical asymptotes; secant and cosecant are drawn from the cosine and sine graphs with bowls touching \(y=\pm1\).

sections.heading: Even and Odd Functions (9.5)
sections.body: A function is even if \(f(-x)=f(x)\) (graph symmetric about the \(y\)-axis) and odd if \(f(-x)=-f(x)\) (symmetric about the origin). Of the six trigonometric functions only \(\cos\) and \(\sec\) are even; \(\sin\), \(\tan\), \(\cot\), \(\csc\) are odd. A product or quotient is even when it has an even number of odd factors; a sum of an even and an odd function is neither.

sections.heading: Sinusoidal Models (9.6)
sections.body: Write a model \(h(t)=a\cos(bt)+d\) or \(a\sin(bt)+d\): midline \(d=\frac{\max+\min}{2}\), amplitude \(|a|=\frac{\max-\min}{2}\), \(b=\frac{2\pi}{T}\) in radians or \(\frac{360^\circ}{T}\) in degrees. A ride starting at the bottom uses \(-\cos\), at the top \(+\cos\), on the midline going up \(+\sin\). A height question has two answers in one cycle.

definitions.definition: \(f(x+p)=f(x)\) for all \(x\) in the domain, for some \(p>0\).
Half the distance between the maximum and the minimum, \(|a|\) for \(a\sin bx\).
The horizontal line \(y=\frac{M+m}{2}\) halfway between the maximum and the minimum.
The horizontal slide \(c\) of the wave \(f[b(x-c)]\).
A vertical line that the graph approaches but never touches, where the function is undefined.
The set of inputs \(x\) for which the function is defined.
The set of outputs \(y\) that the function actually takes.
\(f(-x)=f(x)\); the graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis (cos, sec).
\(f(-x)=-f(x)\); the graph is symmetric about the origin (sin, tan, cot, csc).
A wave of the form \(a\sin[b(x-c)]+d\) or \(a\cos[b(x-c)]+d\).
The number of cycles per second, \(f=\frac{1}{T}\), in hertz.

examTips: Maximum and minimum of \(a+b\sin(\cdot)\) or \(a+b\cos(\cdot)\): \(M=a+|b|\), \(m=a-|b|\). Ignore whatever is inside the bracket.
Period of \(f(ax+b)\): divide the base period by \(|a|\). Base period is \(2\pi\) for sin, cos, sec, csc and \(\pi\) for tan, cot.
Period of a sum: LCM of the numerators over the HCF of the denominators, after writing each period as a fraction.
Before taking a reciprocal, find the maximum and minimum of the denominator. If they have opposite signs there is no maximum or minimum.
Even or odd: count the odd factors. An even count gives an even function. A sum of an even and an odd term is neither.
Only cos and sec are even. sin, tan, cot and csc are odd.
Never join the two branches of tan through an asymptote. The zeros of cot are at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi\), not at \(x=0\).
The greatest value of \(a\cos x+b\sin x\) is \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\).
Word problems: starting at the bottom means \(-\cos\). Amplitude is the radius, not the diameter. Give both times for a height in one cycle.
